# Ensure every Main Street card has dedicated card art (1024×1024 source)

## Problem statement

Every Main Street card renders a square art zone in its top-left corner, but
**108 of the 171 unique cards in `card-data.csv` currently render the same
generic `Fallback` sprite**, so the bulk of the deck is visually
indistinguishable. A player cannot tell an `Upgrade to Patisserie` from a
`Chef` from a `Rainy Day` at a glance, which undermines the 64×64 left-art
redesign's whole purpose.

## Users

- **Player (market / hand / street):** needs to recognise a card by its art
  without reading the title — especially when cards overlap in hand or stack
  on the street.
- **Content author:** needs a documented, testable rule for what art a card
  resolves to, so new cards cannot silently reintroduce `Fallback` art.
- **Engine maintainer:** needs one art-resolution path shared by the runtime
  generator and the static SVG exporter, guarded by a regression test.

User stories:

- As a player, when I look at the market, I can tell any two cards apart by
  their art alone.
- As an upgrade card, I show the art of the business I enhance under my new
  display name, so my purpose is obvious.
- As a content author, when I add a card to `card-data.csv`, the test suite
  tells me if I forgot to give it art.

## Producer decisions (answered 2026-09-26)

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|----------|----------|
| Q1 | Art scope / strategy | **Option A — reuse-first.** Actively **duplicate the existing art under the new (card/display) name**, and produce **new art only where necessary** (no suitable existing art). |
| Q2 | Art production ownership | **The producer will produce the new sprites.** This item still owns the mapping, resolver, regeneration tooling and the drift guard. |
| Q3 | Event mapping granularity | **Map events by `trigger` × `targetSynergy` category** (a documented, generated mapping). |

## Producer decisions (answered 2026-09-29)

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|----------|----------|
| Q4 | Source-art size | The producer provides **1024×1024** source art (`<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`). The “64×64” is the on-card display zone, not the production size. |
| Q5 | Staff art granularity | **One sprite per staff role** (24 sprites). |
| Q6 | Event-category art | **Unique (bespoke) sprite per `(trigger, targetSynergy)` category** — representatives are not reused. |
| Q7 | Drift-guard tightening | **Yes** — tighten the guard to a strict “zero `Fallback` for every card in `card-data.csv`” assertion once the sprites land, in the same change. |
| Q8 | Duplicate-name clash | **Rename to remove the clashes**: business `Florist` → `Flower Shop`; event `Community Garden` → `Garden Party`. |

Art-production ownership (Q2, 2026-09-26) is unchanged: the producer supplies
all new source sprites.

## Existing state (verified 2026-09-26, `dev` @ 933644bc)

Resolution path (all four card families call it with the card's `name`):

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCardArt.ts` → `resolveCardArtName()` /
  `hasDedicatedCardArt()`: (1) spelling alias → (2) exact name → (3)
  `Fallback`.
- Map built by `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs`
  from committed `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` files into
  `example-games/main-street/card-art-map.json`.
- A second consumer, `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`,
  duplicates the alias/lookup logic and must be kept in step.

Verified counts:

- `card-data.csv`: **173 rows / 171 unique names** (duplicate names across
  families: `Florist` = business + staff, `Community Garden` = community-space
  + event → name-keyed resolution shares one sprite).
- Committed sprites: **62 dedicated + `Fallback`** (63 map entries).
- Cards resolving today: **65** (63 exact + 2 via aliases).
- **Cards rendering `Fallback`: 108**:

| Family              | Cards | Resolving | Missing |
|---------------------|------:|----------:|--------:|
| business            |    30 |        28 |       2 |
| community-space     |     8 |         1 |       7 |
| upgrade             |    39 |         0 |      39 |
| staff               |    25 |         1 |      24 |
| event               |    71 |        35 |      36 |
| **Total**           |  **173** | **65** | **108** |

Every missing card already has an `art_notes` description in `card-data.csv`
(the source the existing 1024×1024 sprites were built from). There is **no
in-repo image generator** — the existing sprites were committed out-of-band
(commit `05026750`), and the producer will continue producing new art the same
way.

## Size clarification (reviewed 2026-09-29)

The “64×64” in the original title is the **on-card display zone** — a layout
dimension in SVG user units — **not** the size of the source art to produce.
Code review of the generator and renderer confirms three distinct layers:

| Layer | Size | Where | Role |
|-------|-----:|-------|------|
| On-card art zone | 64×64 | `src/scenes/MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` (`GRAPHIC_*`) | SVG layout box only |
| Embedded bitmap | 256×256 | `src/card-art-map.json` (`artResolution`) | WebP `data:` URI in the SVG |
| **Source art** | **1024×1024** | `src/sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` | Generator input |

`src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` only loads files named
`<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` (`SOURCE_SUFFIX = '_1024_x_1024.png'`) and downscales
each to 256×256 WebP (`ART_RESOLUTION = 256`). Phaser rasterises the card SVG
at `qualityScale = max(4, dpr)`, so the 64×64 zone needs a ≥256×256 bitmap to
stay crisp; a 64×64 source would be stretched ~4× and appear pixelated.

**Produce every new sprite at 1024×1024**, named `<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`, in
`src/sprites/`. The legacy `<Name>_64_x_64.png` files are superseded
thumbnails and are not read by the generator.

## Progress (2026-09-29)

The mapping/resolver/tooling + pending-aware drift guard landed on `dev` as
commit `4b80741` (full unit suite green): `src/card-art-map.json` is now
`version: 3`. Real coverage rose from **65 → 95 of 171** unique cards.

**Duplicate names split (commit `874f419`).** On producer decision Q8 the two
duplicate card names were renamed, so all **173 card names are now unique**:

- business `Florist` → **`Flower Shop`** — keeps the existing rose sprite
  (renamed `Flower Shop_1024_x_1024.png`); its `upgradePath` and
  `Upgrade to Garden Center`'s `targetBusiness` both follow.
- event `Community Garden` → **`Garden Party`** — now needs its own art and maps
  to the `Investment__` category until then.
- staff `Florist` keeps its name; its business restriction is now
  `Flower Shop|Commerce|Culture`.

Card IDs are intentionally unchanged (`biz-florist`, `evt-community-garden`) to
preserve save/challenge compatibility. After the split, **95 of 173** cards
resolve and **78** still render `Fallback`: the staff `Florist` and event
`Garden Party` joined the pending set, giving **46 distinct source sprites** to
produce.

## Desired change (confirmed strategy)

1. **Upgrades (39) — duplicate target art under the new display name.**
   For each `Upgrade to …`, copy the art of its `targetBusiness` to a new
   source sprite named after the upgrade's `newDisplayName` (all 39 are
   distinct, no collisions, and none is already a sprite). Seven targets are
   themselves gaps, so their art must be produced first: `Cafe`,
   `Health Kiosk`, `Laundromat`, `Library`, `Park`, `Playground`,
   `Town Fountain`.
2. **Business / community-space gaps (9) — new art.** `Laundromat`, `Cafe` and
   all community spaces except `Community Garden`: `Park`, `Library`,
   `Playground`, `Town Fountain`, `Health Kiosk`, `Community Shelter`,
   `Public Art`.
3. **Staff (25) — new staff art.** **One sprite per staff role** (confirmed
   2026-09-29), produced by the producer. The split moved `Florist` (staff)
   off the shared business sprite, so all 25 roles need art.
4. **Events (37) — category mapping.** Map each event to a category sprite
   keyed by `(trigger, targetSynergy)`; **unique (bespoke) art per category**
   (confirmed 2026-09-29), produced by the producer. `Garden Party` joined the
   category-mapped set after the split.
5. **Resolver / map.** Extend the generated mapping (and/or `CARD_ART_ALIASES`)
   so both consumers agree and regeneration stays deterministic; keep
   `Fallback` only as the genuine last resort.
6. **Drift guard.** Add a unit test over `card-data.csv` asserting full
   coverage and failing when a new art-less card appears.

## Required art (derived)

| Group | Cards | Mechanism | New sprites |
|-------|------:|-----------|------------:|
| Upgrade | 39 | Duplicate `targetBusiness` art under each upgrade's `newDisplayName` | 0 new (39 copies) |
| Business + community-space gaps | 9 | New source art | 9 |
| Staff | 25 | New source art — one per role | 25 |
| Event | 37 | Unique `(trigger × targetSynergy)` category art — 12 categories | 12 |
| **Total distinct source sprites** | | | **46** |

Event categories for the 36 missing events (representative = an event with
dedicated art today in the same category, available to duplicate):

| `trigger` | `targetSynergy` | Cards | Existing representative |
|-----------|-----------------|------:|-------------------------|
| Incident  | (none)          | 9 | Tax Audit |
| Incident  | Culture         | 1 | Cultural Grant |
| Incident  | Entertainment   | 1 | Noise Complaint |
| Incident  | Food            | 6 | *(none — new)* |
| Incident  | Health          | 1 | *(none — new)* |
| Incident  | Service         | 4 | *(none — new)* |
| Investment| (none)          | 3 | Charity Drive |
| Investment| Commerce        | 1 | Grand Opening Sale |
| Investment| Entertainment   | 3 | Street Performer |
| Investment| Food            | 2 | Harvest Festival |
| Investment| Health          | 3 | *(none — new)* |
| Investment| Service         | 2 | *(none — new)* |

Existing dedicated event art (35 events) is retained; only the 36 missing
events are category-mapped. **The producer confirmed on 2026-09-29 that each of
the 12 categories gets unique (bespoke) art** — the “existing representative”
column above is informational only and is not reused.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every **unique** card name in `card-data.csv` resolves via
   `MainStreetCardArt.hasDedicatedCardArt()` to a **non-`Fallback`** sprite
   (documented alias/category mapping counts); currently 65/171.
2. All 39 upgrade cards resolve to art duplicated from their `targetBusiness`
   under the upgrade's `newDisplayName`; no upgrade renders `Fallback`.
3. All 24 staff cards resolve to dedicated staff art; no staff card renders
   `Fallback`.
4. All 36 missing event cards resolve to a documented
   `(trigger, targetSynergy)` category sprite; no event card renders `Fallback`.
5. All 9 business / community-space gaps resolve to dedicated art; no card in
   either family renders `Fallback`.
6. A unit-test drift guard over `card-data.csv` asserts AC 1–5 and fails when a
   new card is added without art; `Fallback` remains in the map and resolver for
   genuinely-unknown/future cards (the existing "unknown card" test still passes).
7. Both consumers of `card-art-map.json` (runtime `MainStreetCardArt.ts` and
   `scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`) apply the identical mapping;
   regeneration via `scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` is
   deterministic and reproducible.
8. `docs/main-street/card-dimensions.md` and `public/assets/CREDITS.md`
   document the mapping rules and the licence/attribution of any new art.
9. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
10. `npm run build` is green and the **full project test suite must pass** with
    the new changes.

## Constraints

- New art must be permissively licensed (CC0 / MIT / Apache 2.0) and attributed
  in `public/assets/CREDITS.md`.
- Source art remains `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`; `card-art-map.json`
  stays generated (never hand-edited).
- No change to the 64×64 zone geometry, the 140×80 card size, the 256×256
  embedded WebP format, or the SVG being self-contained (inline `data:` URI).
- Mapping logic must be expressed once and consumed by both the runtime and the
  static generator.

## Desired artefacts

- Up to 45 new `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` source files (9 business /
  community-space, 24 staff, up to 12 event categories) and 39 upgrade
  duplicates named by `newDisplayName`.
- Updated generated mapping + resolver.
- Drift-guard unit test in `tests/main-street/`.
- Docs + credits updates.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCardArt.ts` — resolver: targetBusiness /
  category resolution or extended alias path.
- `example-games/main-street/card-art-map.json` — regenerated mapping (data).
- `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` —
  derive the upgrade-duplication and event-category mapping from
  `card-data.csv` + sprites.
- `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs` —
  second consumer; mirror the mapping.
- `example-games/main-street/sprites/` — new + duplicated `_1024_x_1024.png`
  source art (producer).
- `tests/main-street/card-art.test.ts` — add the `card-data.csv` drift guard.
- `docs/main-street/card-dimensions.md` — document mapping rules.
- `public/assets/CREDITS.md` — licence/attribution for new art.

## Risks / assumptions

- **Art-availability dependency:** the resolver/tooling can land independently,
  but AC 1–5 cannot pass until the producer's sprites are committed. Plan
  should sequence tooling + drift guard first, art last.
- **Duplicate-name collision (resolved 2026-09-29):** the business `Florist`
  and the event `Community Garden` were renamed to `Flower Shop` and
  `Garden Party` (Q8), so every card name is now unique and no sprite is shared
  across families. IDs are unchanged for save/challenge compatibility.
- **Category-art fidelity (resolved 2026-09-29):** the producer confirmed
  unique (bespoke) art for all 12 event categories, so no representative
  sprite is reused.
- **Dual-consumer drift risk:** `generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs` duplicates
  the alias logic; a mapping change that misses it silently diverges — assert
  both in tests.
- **Scope-creep risk:** "improve the existing 62 sprites" and "redesign the art
  zone" are out of scope — record separately if they surface.
- **Assumption:** `hasDedicatedCardArt()` remains name-keyed; any targetBusiness
  indirection is baked into the generated map so the public API is unchanged.

## Out of scope

- Changing the 64×64 left-art geometry or the 140×80 card dimensions.
- New card types or `card-data.csv` content changes (beyond `art_notes` if new
  art needs them).
- Filling the empty gameplay `description` column on the 45 `event` rows
  (unrelated to art; all 173 rows already carry `art_notes`).
- Redesigning/replacing the existing 62 dedicated sprites.
- Adding an in-repo image-generation tool (the producer supplies the art).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 "Art scope / strategy: how much new art vs. mapping/reuse for the 108
  cards?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-26):** Option A — actively duplicate
  the current art using the new name; new art where necessary. Source:
  interactive producer reply.
- Q2 "Art production ownership & pipeline: who produces the new sprites, and
  does this item ship mapping machinery first?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-09-26):** "I will produce them." Source: interactive producer reply.
  Research: no in-repo sprite generator exists (last sprite commit
  `05026750`, external).
- Q3 "Event mapping granularity: what taxonomy, and is a category sprite
  acceptable for AC4?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-26):**
  `trigger` × `targetSynergy` categories. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q1 prior/open record superseded by the answers above (was OPEN QUESTION).
- Q4 "Source-art size: 64×64 or 1024×1024?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-09-29):** the producer provides **1024×1024** source art; the 64×64 is
  the on-card display zone. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q5 "Staff art granularity: per-role or shared?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-09-29):** **one sprite per role**. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q6 "Event-category art: reuse a representative or unique?" — **Answer
  (producer, 2026-09-29):** **unique** per category. Source: interactive
  producer reply.
- Q7 "Tighten the drift guard to strict zero-`Fallback` once art lands?" —
  **Answer (producer, 2026-09-29):** **yes**. Source: interactive producer
  reply.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MP1QZC6Q005EMEZ** – Asset generation: placeholder SVGs for new cards (completed)
- **CG-0MLTFDAYD0J6KLY3** – Phaser Scene Static Card Layout (completed)
- **CG-0MPD5XALT007F1WV** – Gym Graphics: Card Flip Animation (DeckRng + HandPile) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: 0mtorj5fs006b0un, acceptance, add, alias, apache (+136 more)
- `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-2.md` — matched: acceptance, add, approach, art, asserts (+107 more)

# Intake Brief: Serial Seller: achievement manifest entry + Steamworks API name

## Problem Statement

The new **Serial Seller** challenge (`ch-serial-seller`) must map to a persistent Steam achievement like the existing 12 challenges. The challenge-side mapping is added in the parent item (MS-0MUI7ZJK8003HY9J); this item covers the cross-repo pieces required before the parent can be reviewed.

## Users

- **Producers**: Need the Steam achievement registered on the Steamworks partner backend.
- **Developers**: Need the manifest entry to exist before the drift guard test will pass.
- **Players**: Need the Serial Seller achievement to appear in-game alongside the existing 12 achievements.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `core/electron/achievement-manifest.json` contains a `serial-seller` entry with `steamApiName: TCE_MAIN_STREET_SERIAL_SELLER` and `hidden: false`.
2. The Steamworks partner backend declares the matching `TCE_MAIN_STREET_SERIAL_SELLER` achievement API name.
3. The `core` submodule pointer in the main-street repo is bumped to the commit containing the manifest change.
4. The manifest drift guard (`tests/main-street/main-street-achievements.test.ts`) passes with the parent's mapping in place.
5. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
6. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The manifest lives in the `core` git submodule (a separate repository: `TheWizardsCode/Tableau-Card-Engine`), requiring two repo operations.
- The `steamApiName` values must match exactly what is configured on the Steamworks partner backend, or Steam will silently drop the unlock.
- The achievement must not be hidden (`hidden: false`), consistent with the existing 12 challenges.
- The Steamworks backend configuration is a producer/external action that must be completed independently of code changes.

## Existing State

- 12 existing achievements in `core/electron/achievement-manifest.json`, all with the pattern `TCE_MAIN_STREET_<UPPER_SNAKE_CASE>`.
- The manifest is validated by `validateAchievementManifest()` and the drift guard test.
- Precedent: MS-0MUMAZTAY00515MC (bumping core submodule pointer).

## Desired Change

- Add one entry to the manifest for the Serial Seller achievement.
- Commit to the core repo and bump the submodule pointer in main-street.
- Coordinate with the producer to register the achievement on Steamworks.

## Key Files (Predicted)

- `core/electron/achievement-manifest.json` — Add `serial-seller` entry
- `core/` (git submodule) — Commit the manifest change
- `.gitmodules` / submodule index — Bump the submodule pointer

## Related Work

- **MS-0MUI7ZJK8003HY9J**: Sell 3 businesses challenge (parent, blocked by this item)
- **MS-0MUNO0M2I004TK04**: Wire Main Street challenges to Steam achievements (parent epic)
- **MS-0MUMAZTAY00515MC**: Precedent for bumping core submodule pointer

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Steamworks backend delay**: If the producer has not yet registered the achievement on Steamworks, the achievement will not unlock for players even after code changes land. This is tracked as a separate action.
- **Scope creep**: Additional achievement metadata (e.g., icons, descriptions) may be desired later; record as a follow-up, not in scope for this item.
- **Submodule conflict**: Unlikely but possible if the core repo has concurrent changes; resolve by rebasing on latest core before bumping.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- This item was already sufficiently defined; no interview questions were asked. The description, scope, and acceptance criteria were clear and actionable.

## Dependency & audit resolution (2026-10-01)

Producer confirmed the Steamworks backend registration (AC2) is not yet done and requires a dependency chain. Two dependency items were created in the core project (CG store — the correct home for Steamworks backend work; worklog does not support cross-store dependency edges, so they are recorded here as cross-project references):

- **CG-0MUPMJVS90019KSQ** — Create the Steamworks project for Tableau Card Engine
- **CG-0MUPN2I7K003KNL1** — Register Main Street achievements on the Steamworks backend *(depends on CG-0MUPMJVS90019KSQ)*

**AC2 therefore remains unmet until CG-0MUPN2I7K003KNL1 completes.** This item carries the `do-not-delegate` tag while externally blocked so the downtime worker does not re-dispatch it.

**Merge state:** the item's work is integrated into `dev`/`origin/dev` as commit `dd11ea4` (core → `d2d1f322`). The stale feature branch (which referenced the superseded core commit `4a287d4`) was reset to `dd11ea4`.

**AC4 call:** the drift guard requires the parent challenge-side mapping from **MS-0MUI7ZJK8003HY9J** (which depends on this item, so no cycle is possible). AC4 is verified at parent integration time; the mapping is present uncommitted in the working tree today and will pass permanently once the parent lands.

## Plan review — 2026-11-05 (verified state)

Verified against the current checkout: main-street `dev` at `f4f083ed`, `core` submodule pinned at `5a16c2fb`, superproject working tree clean.

- **AC1 met** — `core/electron/achievement-manifest.json` contains `achievementId: serial-seller` with `steamApiName: TCE_MAIN_STREET_SERIAL_SELLER` and `hidden: false` (13 entries in total).
- **AC3 met** — the `core` pointer now pins `5a16c2fb`, later than the `d2d1f322` recorded above, and that commit contains the manifest entry.
- **AC4 preconditions satisfied** — the parent mapping (MS-0MUI7ZJK8003HY9J) is now **committed**, not uncommitted as stated above: `src/MainStreetAchievements.ts` maps all 13 challenges, and the manifest and the game-side mapping agree exactly (13 ↔ 13, no drift in either direction). `tests/main-street/main-street-achievements.test.ts` is the guard that exercises this.
- **AC2 unmet / external** — unchanged: blocked on `CG-0MUPN2I7K003KNL1` (Steamworks backend registration). Not verifiable from the repository.
- **AC5** — no documentation change beyond the manifest entry was identified as required; the existing 12-achievement pattern is followed.
- **AC6** — enforced by the dev-push gate; not re-run by this planning session.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-11-05 — Plan re-run (effort Extra Small / Low, so decomposition skipped): six review stages run, AC coverage 100% (proceed), stage set to `plan_complete`. Recorded the verified AC state above; no child work items created.

# Remote hosting of card packs (remote bundle source) — Intake Brief

## Problem statement

Card packs are currently discovered from a single source: a content directory
(the Electron launcher) or, since `MS-0MV1O7EGG004MWGD` landed, a bundled
build-time registry (the browser). There is no mechanism for hosting a pack
catalogue remotely, so publishing or updating a pack forces a rebuild and
re-release of the game. This item implements the **remote source provider** on
top of the pack-source registry abstraction (`PackSource[]` /
`PackSourceRegistry`) introduced by `MS-0MV1O7EGG004MWGD`.

## Users

- **Distribution operator** — hosts a signed pack catalogue at a URL and
  expects packs to appear in players' Card Packs panels without rebuilding the
  game.
- **Main Street player** — experiences remote packs identically to bundled
  packs (lock → purchase → enable → deal) and continues to play offline on
  bundled packs when the remote host is unreachable.

Example user stories:

> As a distribution operator, I want to host a card pack catalogue at a URL
> that the game verifies with a signed manifest, so I can publish or update
> packs for an installed game without rebuilding the launcher or the web build.

> As a player, I want remote packs to appear in my Card Packs panel and behave
> exactly like bundled packs, while the game still boots and plays offline on
> bundled packs if the remote host is unreachable.

## Locked design decisions (producer, 2026-10-17)

- **Q1 — Configuration: build-time config constant.** Remote source URLs are
  declared in a build-time config constant (e.g. an environment variable read
  by `vite.config.ts` / a config module), matching the bundled-source pattern.
  No runtime URL mutation in this iteration; launcher-supplied or well-known
  URLs are a possible follow-up.
- **Q2 — Integrity: signed manifests (Ed25519).** Remote manifests are signed
  (Ed25519); the game verifies the signature against a pinned public key before
  trusting any remote pack content. A manifest that fails verification is
  rejected whole (no packs from that source) with a logged warning — safe
  refusal, never a crash. Host allow-list remains as the first gate (only
  configured URLs are fetched at all).
- **Q3 — Timeout & degradation: bounded hard timeout, console-only warning.**
  A hard fetch timeout (≈3 s) bounds the boot path; on failure the game boots
  on bundled packs and logs a warning to the console. **No UI change** — no
  toast, no panel indicator. The Card Packs listing is never empty when a
  bundled pack exists.
- **Q4 — Merge precedence: bundled always wins.** When the same pack id
  appears in more than one source, the **bundled source wins**; a remote pack
  can never override bundled core content. This is implemented by keeping the
  bundled source registered *before* the remote source in the registry (the
  registry's first-wins consultation order) plus an explicit test asserting the
  precedence.

## Scope

1. **Remote source provider.** Implement a `PackSource` (`createRemotePackSource`)
   that fetches a pack manifest and pack CSVs from a configured base URL via
   the loader's existing `fetchManifest` / `fetchCsv` transport seam and
   contributes its packs to the merged pool.
2. **Configuration.** Declare remote source URLs as a build-time config
   constant (e.g. `VITE_REMOTE_PACK_URL` or a config module), consumed when the
   default registry is built. Multiple remote sources compose additively in
   registration order, always **after** the bundled source.
3. **Merge and precedence.** Pack-id precedence is deterministic: bundled wins
   over remote (remote registered after bundled). Pack-id conflicts between two
   remote sources resolve first-wins (registration order). The core merge
   contract continues to reject duplicate card ids whole.
4. **Gating.** Remote packs remain content-unlock gated; the unlock target key
   and the scoped simulated-purchase flow apply unchanged. Remote packs are not
   automatically ungated.
5. **Degradation.** A remote host that is slow, unreachable, or serving a
   malformed manifest degrades to the bundled/static packs with a warning —
   never blocks boot, never blanks the listing. A bounded timeout (≈3 s) is
   applied to the manifest fetch (and per-file fetches).
6. **Trust and integrity.** Remote manifests are **Ed25519-signed**; the game
   verifies the signature against a pinned public key before trusting content.
   Failure modes: bad signature / missing signature / malformed manifest →
   reject source whole with a warning. Host allow-list: only configured URLs
   are fetched.
7. **Caching / offline.** No client-side caching of remote packs in this
   iteration — remote packs require the remote host at load time; the offline
   story is the bundled packs. Cache in `localStorage` / Cache Storage is a
   recorded follow-up.
8. **Docs and tests.** Cover remote discovery, signed-manifest verification,
   degradation, gating, precedence and asset resolution with tests; document
   the remote-hosting contract (configuration, signing, hosting layout,
   degradation).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Remote discovery.** A pack catalogue hosted at a configured (build-time)
   URL is fetched at runtime and its packs appear in the Card Packs panel
   alongside bundled packs.
2. **Parity.** Remote packs behave identically to bundled packs across the full
   lock → purchase → enable → deal flow, including save/load persistence.
3. **Degradation.** When the remote host is unreachable, slow, or serves a
   malformed manifest, the game boots on bundled packs and logs a warning; the
   Card Packs listing is never empty when a bundled pack exists; the fetch is
   bounded by a timeout (≈3 s) so boot is never blocked.
4. **Rejection of bad data.** A malformed remote manifest or a pack with a bad
   header/duplicate id is rejected whole with a logged warning, without
   affecting packs from other sources.
5. **Deterministic precedence.** Bundled packs always win over remote packs
   with the same pack id; conflicts between remote sources resolve
   first-wins in registration order; precedence is explicit and tested.
6. **Signed-manifest integrity.** A remote manifest whose Ed25519 signature is
   missing, invalid, or not produced by the pinned key is rejected whole with a
   logged warning and no packs from that source are loaded; the failure mode is
   documented.
7. **Asset resolution.** Remote pack art resolves and renders correctly,
   coordinated with `MS-0MV26K321003MWO0` (pack assets self-contained) — remote
   assets resolve through the environment-injected `LoadedCardPack.assetUrls`
   seam.
8. **Documentation.** README / packs README / DEPLOYMENT documentation covers
   remote configuration, the hosting contract (layout, signing), integrity and
   degradation.
9. **Testing.** Full project test suite passes with the new changes; remote
   discovery, signature verification, degradation, precedence, gating and asset
   resolution are covered by automated tests.

## Constraints

- **Reuse existing seams.** The remote source consumes the existing injectable
  `fetchManifest` / `fetchCsv` / `fetchAsset` transports on the loader
  (`createPackSourceTransports`); no core loader changes.
- **Totality.** The remote source never throws: network failures, timeouts,
  malformed responses, signature failures, and missing files all resolve to
  `null` and the core loader degrades to bundled/static packs.
- **Additive.** The remote source is added to the existing
  `PackSourceRegistry` **after** the bundled source, without modifying bundled
  or content-directory sources.
- **Bounded timeout.** Remote fetches on the boot path are bounded (≈3 s) so
  the game never stalls waiting for a slow or hung host.
- **Signing key separation.** The pinned verification public key is a build-time
  constant; the private signing key is held by the distribution operator and is
  never shipped in the game.
- **Pack content stays licence-clean.** Remote packs must satisfy the same
  licence requirements as bundled packs (documented in the hosting contract).
- **No runtime URL mutation** in this iteration (build-time config only).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/MainStreetPackSources.ts` — `createRemotePackSource`, signature
  verification, registration and precedence.
- `src/MainStreetCardPacks.ts` — remote source configuration + transport
  wiring (consumes the `packSources` option).
- `vite.config.ts` / config module (e.g. `src/mainStreetRemotePacks.ts`) —
  build-time remote URL + pinned public key declaration.
- `src/MainStreetLifecycleManagerLifecycle.ts` — remote source boot wiring.
- `core/src/ui/CardPackLoader.ts` — transport usage (should not need changes).
- `tests/main-street/` — remote discovery, signature verification, degradation,
  precedence, asset-resolution tests.
- `README.md`, `packs/README.md`, `DEPLOYMENT.md` — remote-hosting contract.

## Out of scope

- A pack storefront, purchase/checkout, or pack-authoring UI.
- A pack CDN/build-publish pipeline or signing tooling UI (a natural follow-up
  — the signing key/algorithm contract is defined here, tooling later).
- Real money/Steam storefront transactions.
- Changing the bundled or content-directory sources.
- Client-side caching of remote packs for offline use (recorded follow-up).
- Runtime/launcher-supplied remote URL mutation (build-time config only).

## Related work

- **`MS-0MV1O7EGG004MWGD`** — Make card packs available in the browser
  distribution: provides `PackSource` / `PackSourceRegistry`; **blocks** this
  item (this item depends on it). Completed and shipped.
- **`MS-0MV26K321003MWO0`** — Make card-pack assets self-contained: pack art
  resolves from pack assets; remote assets must consume the
  `LoadedCardPack.assetUrls` seam. Completed and shipped.
- **`MS-0MV0M5BHH0020WFY`** — Add a DLC to test the pack unlock and import:
  parent context for the DLC channel.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — supply chain.** Remote content is untrusted; a hostile pack could
  inject arbitrary card data. *Mitigation:* Ed25519-signed manifests verified
  against a pinned public key; host allow-list; safe refusal (reject whole,
  log warning, never crash).
- **Risk — signing overhead.** Key management, signing tooling, and
  verification bugs. *Mitigation:* verification is a small, isolated,
  well-tested function; private key never ships; the public key is pinned at
  build time; signing tooling can be a follow-up (the contract is defined).
- **Risk — boot latency.** A remote fetch on the boot path could stall the
  game. *Mitigation:* bounded timeout (≈3 s), non-blocking degradation,
  bundled-first registry order.
- **Risk — offline regression.** A user who once fetched a remote pack cannot
  use it offline. *Mitigation:* explicit decision — no remote caching this
  iteration; bundled packs remain the offline story; caching recorded as a
  follow-up.
- **Risk — scope creep.** Caching, signing tooling, runtime URL mutation, and a
  pack CDN are natural follow-ups. *Mitigation:* recorded as out of scope /
  linked follow-ups, not built here.
- **Assumption — registry seam exists.** `MS-0MV1O7EGG004MWGD` provides the
  `PackSource` abstraction; this item adds a provider rather than
  re-architecting.
- **Assumption — transport seams are adequate.** The existing
  `fetchManifest` / `fetchCsv` / `fetchAsset` transports can serve a remote
  source without core changes.
- **Assumption — Ed25519 available.** A small Ed25519 verification
  implementation (e.g. WebCrypto `crypto.subtle`/`Ed25519`, or a tiny
  dependency) is available in the browser and test environments; the exact
  mechanism is an implementation detail the implementer records.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Configuration mechanism** (how remote source URLs are declared:
  build-time constant / launcher setting / well-known URL). — **Answer
  (producer, interactive reply, 2026-10-17): A — build-time config constant.**
  Matches the bundled-source pattern; simplest; runtime URL mutation is a
  recorded follow-up. Source: worklog comment `MS-C0MVC8TJJA0030X19`.
- **Q2 — Pack-integrity model** (host allow-list / allow-list + checksum /
  signed manifests). — **Answer (producer, interactive reply, 2026-10-17):
  C — signed manifests (Ed25519).** Verification against a pinned public key;
  failure rejects the source whole with a warning. Source: worklog comment
  `MS-C0MVC8TJJA0030X19`.
- **Q3 — Timeout and degradation behaviour** (hard timeout + console only /
  + toast / + panel indicator). — **Answer (producer, interactive reply,
  2026-10-17): A — hard timeout (≈3 s), console warning, no UI change.**
  Source: worklog comment `MS-C0MVC8TJJA0030X19`.
- **Q4 — Merge precedence** for the same pack id across sources (bundled wins /
  last wins / first wins). — **Answer (producer, interactive reply,
  2026-10-17): A — bundled always wins.** Remote packs never override bundled
  core content; implemented via registry order + explicit test. Source:
  worklog comment `MS-C0MVC8TJJA0030X19`.

# Finish gate: a lagging engine pin can fail the build itself when `engine:sync` advances past a breaking engine API change

Discovered during **MS-0MVTEVK8S0078QC4** (AC1 verification of **MS-0MVSB1OVW00178W6**), while reproducing the lagging-pin condition. Verification only: nothing was worked around; this item records the gap.

## What happens

`implement.py finish` runs `npm run build`, which starts with `engine:sync`. When the worktree's committed pin lags the engine tracked tip, `engine:sync` advances `./core` to the tip **before** `tsc --noEmit` / `vite build` run — so the build compiles the item's source against an engine the source was never written for.

Reproduced on a throwaway worktree at `a6ef0b7d` (pinned `21bedf7a`; engine `dev` tip `2305f888`), which still uses the pre-rename `hasChoices` manifest flag:

```
engine:sync: core updated 21bedf7a8c → 2305f888d0
src/MainStreetStorylineContentAdapter.ts(88,5): error TS2353: Object literal may only specify known properties, and 'hasChoices' does not exist in type 'ContentFieldMapping'.
tests/main-street/MainStreetStorylineContentAdapter.test.ts(194,44): error TS2551: Property 'hasChoices' does not exist on type 'ManifestNode'. Did you mean 'isChoice'?
npm run build → exit 2
```

The build-churn exclusion (`SA-0MVZE164P0048306`) cannot help: it runs **after** a successful build. The same probe at `99489ad8` (pin still `21bedf7a`, but source already at `isChoice`) built cleanly and the exclusion worked as designed.

## Why it matters

The parent epic's user story is that a documentation- or evidence-only item must not be blocked by an unrelated engine bump. Today the re-pin no longer reaches the commit, but the build still runs against the advanced engine first, so an older worktree can fail to build for a reason the item never caused — and the failure arrives as a plain build error, not as an engine-composition condition.

## Options (not decided here)

- (A) Report the condition explicitly: when the pre-build pin lags the engine tip, record it in the finish report and the build-failure message ("build ran against engine <tip>, item pinned <sha> — the advance is not part of the commit"), so the operator can tell an engine-induced build failure from a source failure.
- (B) Build against the pinned composition: restore the pin/gitlink *before* the build and re-sync only when the item itself changes composition (needs producer sign-off — it touches the pin policy `CG-0MVO268500071BPI`).
- (C) Leave as-is and document it as an accepted limitation of syncing at build time.

Option (B) is the closest to remedy C (verify-only `engine:sync`), which the producer already rejected for the finish gate, so it must not be adopted silently.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The condition "pre-build pin lags the engine tracked tip and the build failed" is visible in the finish report and the build-failure comment, naming both SHAs.
- [ ] A published limitation note exists in `docs/dev/testing.md` / the implement skill reference if the behaviour is kept.
- [ ] No cache-key or pin-policy change without producer sign-off.

## Plan decision (2026-11-03)

**Option (A) adopted — keep the build-time sync, make the condition explicit — together with the documentation half of Option (C).** The item's own draft AC1 requires exactly this (both SHAs in the finish report *and* the build-failure comment), and AC3 forbids a cache-key or pin-policy change without sign-off. **Option (B) is explicitly not adopted:** it changes build composition and touches pin policy `CG-0MVO268500071BPI`, so it requires producer sign-off and must not be implemented as a side effect of this bug.

Assumptions recorded (not invented requirements):

- **Repository boundary (precedent Q1=A on `MS-0MVSB1OVW00178W6`):** the finish report and the build-failure comment are produced by `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` in **SorraAgents**, which this repository must not edit. The framework change is therefore filed as `SA-0MW06FLFR009F0P4` and this item tracks the documentation plus the verification of that change.
- **The advance is on stdout.** `engine:sync` logs `core updated <from> → <to>` to stdout, while the build-failure comment currently posts only `stderr[:500]` — so the failure path can name both SHAs without any change to `engine-sync.mjs`.
- **"If the behaviour is kept"** in draft AC2 is read as: the sync-at-build-time behaviour is kept (Option A/C), so the limitation note is a firm deliverable.

## Plan status (2026-11-04 re-plan)

The plan below still holds; **no new children were needed**. This pass refreshed it against
the changed world (the framework item landed) and advanced the stage to `plan_complete`.

| Parent AC | Delivered by | State |
|---|---|---|
| AC1 — condition visible in the finish report *and* the build-failure comment, both SHAs | `MS-0MW06G151000YJJQ` | `open` / `intake_complete` — **unblocked**, ready to implement |
| AC2 — published limitation note | `MS-0MW06G46Y008R01Q` | `completed` / `in_review` (`d87f99d8`), note verified at `docs/dev/testing.md:732` |
| AC3 — no cache-key or pin-policy change without sign-off | `MS-0MW06G151000YJJQ` | part of the same verification child (diff read of the framework commit) |

What changed since the 2026-11-03 plan:

- **The cross-store blocker is satisfied.** `SA-0MW06FLFR009F0P4` is `completed` / `in_review`
  with commit `e2e2d24ca`, which **is** an ancestor of `origin/dev` in SorraAgents;
  `engine_lag` is present in both the checkout and the installed runtime copy. Nothing
  cleared the verification child's `blocked` state automatically, so this pass re-checked
  and recorded the unblock evidence on that child.
- **One unknown from the effort/risk report is resolved:** the report field name settled as
  `engine_lag` (`report["steps"]["build"]["engine_lag"]`, with
  `submodules[].pinned_sha` / `composed_sha` / `advanced` and a top-level `advanced`), so the
  verification child's AC now names the exact keys instead of "both SHAs".
- **The live lagging-pin state was recorded for the implementer:** `dev` HEAD `dc42eae3`
  pins `d46eb242` while the engine tracked tip is `b3cf4877` (6 commits ahead), so a fresh
  throwaway worktree at `dev` HEAD starts lagging. Reproducing a *build failure* (not just
  an advance) additionally needs source predating a breaking engine API change — the
  recorded `a6ef0b7d` / `21bedf7a` `hasChoices` → `isChoice` seed.
- **Observed state, not acted on:** the main checkout carries a **staged** pin/gitlink
  advance (`configs/engine-pin.json` + `core`, `d46eb242` → `b3cf4877`) left behind by an
  earlier session. This planning run made no commit, no stash, no revert and no reset; the
  verification child's probe worktree must be created from committed `HEAD` so that advance
  never becomes part of an evidence commit.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-11-03 — planned by the `plan` skill (session claim, no assignee hold). Draft ACs adopted as final ACs; plan decision and assumptions recorded above.
- 2026-11-03 — filed the SorraAgents framework item `SA-0MW06FLFR009F0P4` (cross-repo convention as with `SA-0MVZE164P0048306`).
- 2026-11-03 — created children in test-first order: `MS-0MW06G151000YJJQ` (AC1 + AC3 verification, blocked on `SA-0MW06FLFR009F0P4`), `MS-0MW06G46Y008R01Q` (AC2 docs note, unblocked).
- 2026-11-04 — re-planned (stage had regressed to `intake_complete`). Children reused, none created or closed. Verification child `MS-0MW06G151000YJJQ` description refreshed: cross-store blocker recorded as satisfied with commit `e2e2d24ca`, AC tightened to the settled `engine_lag` field keys, no-false-diagnosis AC re-pointed at the named fixture tests, live lagging-pin facts and the failing-build reproduction seed added. Docs child `MS-0MW06G46Y008R01Q` AC2 re-verified in place. Stage → `plan_complete`.

## Evidence

- Probe JSON: `/tmp/ms0mvtevk8-ac1-probe.json` (clean run at `99489ad8`).
- Failing build log: `/tmp/ms0mvtevk8-ac1-probe-build.log` (base `a6ef0b7d`).

**Headline:** Add a persisted *Auto advance turn* setting that either ends the day
automatically when the player can no longer act, or — when off (default) — explains the
out-of-actions state in a dialog that offers to turn the setting on.

## Problem statement

When a player has spent their last action point the game offers no explanation and no
shortcut to progress: they must notice the red `0 actions left` counter and find the
**End Turn** button themselves. Add a persisted **Auto advance turn** setting that
either ends the turn automatically or, when off (the default), explains the situation in
a dialog that also lets the player turn the setting on.

## Users

- **New / casual solo player** — does not yet know that a day ends only when they press
  **End Turn**, and does not know that some staff cards grant extra action points.
  - *As a new player who has just spent my last action, I want to be told why I can no
    longer act and how to continue, so that the game never feels stuck.*
  - *As a player who understands the loop, I want the turn to advance on its own once I
    have nothing left to do, so that I stop clicking End Turn 8+ times a game.*
- **Experienced player** — wants to opt in once and never see the dialog again.
- **Competitive player** — the same out-of-actions moment exists on a human seat during a
  shared day; auto-advance must hand the day to the AI seats exactly as a manual
  **End Turn** does.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Setting exists and is exposed in the settings menu.** A boolean preference
   (`Auto advance turn`) defaults to **false**, persists across sessions in
   `localStorage`, and is rendered as a toggle in the in-game Settings panel alongside the
   existing `Tooltips` / `Reduced Motion` toggles. Toggling it in either place (panel or
   dialog checkbox) updates the same stored preference.
2. **Auto advance on — trigger is the spent-last-action moment (producer decision, Q1 = B).**
   The trigger fires when the player's action budget reaches zero as an action resolves: after
   the action that spends the last action point, and only once that action's animations and
   audio have completed (never mid-animation). With the setting enabled the trigger performs
   the *same* operation as clicking **End Turn** — identical phase flow,
   income/incident/event-choice resolution, turn-summary presentation and save/checkpoint
   behaviour — and fires **at most once per turn** (no double advance, no re-entrant
   end-turn while `uiPhase === 'animating'`).
3. **Dialog when off — same trigger.** With the setting disabled the same spent-last-action
   trigger (again after animations/audio complete) opens a dialog that
   states the player has no action points left, that certain kinds of employed staff grant
   extra action points, and that they must break for the weekend by pressing **End Turn**.
   The dialog offers an **End Turn** button, a **Dismiss** affordance that returns the
   player to the market phase, and a checkbox (unchecked by default) reading
   `[ ] Automatically end my turn when I run out of actions`; checking it persists the
   preference immediately (so the next out-of-actions moment auto-advances).
4. **Non-intrusive.** The dialog fires at most once per turn (re-opening only on a later
   turn), is presented once the action's animations/audio have completed rather than on top
   of them, and never appears while a modal overlay (turn summary, loan offer, event
   choice) is already open. Dismissing it leaves the player in the market phase with the
   **End Turn** button available, so the action-free operations that remain after the last
   action (discarding a hand card, selling, researching the market, opening the journal)
   stay reachable for a player who declines the auto-advance.
5. **Mode guards.** Auto-advance never fires during the tutorial unless the current
   tutorial step is `end-turn` (respecting `isTutorialActionAllowed('end-turn')`), never
   while it is not the human seat's turn in competitive play, and never during
   `uiPhase` values where **End Turn** is not offered (e.g. `placing-from-hand`,
   `event-selected`, `applicant`).
6. **Tests.** Unit tests cover the preference default/persistence and the once-per-turn
   latch; browser tests cover (a) auto-advance ending the turn exactly once, (b) the
   dialog appearing when the setting is off, (c) the checkbox persisting the preference
   and the panel toggle reflecting it, (d) the tutorial/competitive guards, and (e) the
   trigger waiting for the last action's animation to complete.
7. **Documentation.** `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` (settings toggle inventory) and
   `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` §6.0 (action economy) are updated to describe
   the setting and the out-of-actions behaviour. All related documentation (code comments,
   README where relevant) is updated to reflect the changes.
8. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **`core/` is a git submodule** of the Tableau Card Engine
  (`TheWizardsCode/Tableau-Card-Engine`, tracked branch `dev`, pinned by
  `configs/engine-pin.json`). The Settings panel lives in the engine
  (`core/src/ui/SettingsPanel.ts`, `core/src/ui/CardGameScene.ts`), so exposing the
  toggle there needs a **generic, game-agnostic** engine change (e.g. a
  `extraToggles?: { label, get, set }[]` config) committed in the engine repo, followed by
  an `npm run engine:sync` re-pin in this repo. Engine work must not hard-code Main Street
  concepts.
- Preference storage must follow the existing `src/MainStreetPrefs.ts` pattern
  (injectable `StorageLike`, best-effort failure handling) so unit tests run in Node.
- Dialog presentation must follow the existing overlay conventions used by
  `showBuyAndPlacePremiumDialog` (backdrop depth 199, box 200, elements 201, registered in
  `s.overlayObjects`, parented into `hudContainer`) — no new ad-hoc depth values.
- Zero-action gating currently exists at several call sites
  (`MainStreetTurnControllerMarketActions`, `MainStreetTurnControllerDragDrop`,
  `MainStreetMarketSell`, `MainStreetMarketPurchase`). Those remain legality checks for
  illegal attempts; the new behaviour is a **single post-action trigger** and must not be
  duplicated per site.
- The trigger must run only after the triggering action's animations **and** audio have
  completed — it cannot be bolted onto the raw state mutation, because the player would
  see the turn end underneath a playing animation.
- CHANGELOG.md is out of scope (managed by the ship/release pipeline).

## Existing state

- `src/MainStreetPrefs.ts` already stores game-specific preferences in `localStorage`
  (`tce-main-street-buy-and-place-premium-dialog-dismissed`,
  `tce-main-street-enabled-card-packs`) with an injectable storage adapter.
- `core/src/ui/SettingsPanel.ts` renders toggles for Mute, Tooltips, Reduced Motion,
  difficulty, card design, end-turn keybind and (dev-only) Debug Tools; the panel is
  configured through `SettingsPanelConfig` and created by
  `CardGameScene.initSettingsPanel(...)`, which `MainStreetScene` overrides.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts#showBuyAndPlacePremiumDialog` is the closest
  precedent: a modal explainer with a persisted "Don't show this again" checkbox.
- Out-of-actions feedback today is a transient `flashError` string —
  `'No actions remaining this week. End your turn to start next week.'` — raised from
  `onBusinessCardClick`, `onMarketRefresh`, staff-move handlers, drag-drop guards and the
  market legality helpers.
- The HUD shows `N actions left (M banked)` in the action cluster above the **End Turn**
  button; the End Turn handler is `MainStreetTurnController.endTurn()` →
  `endTurn(tcCtx)` in `MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts`, which already implements the
  tutorial gate, the banking hint and the competitive hand-off.
- Playing with zero actions is still deliberately possible at a premium (same-turn
  buy-and-place costs +50%), and several operations are action-free (discard, sell,
  research market, journal).

## Desired change

1. `src/MainStreetPrefs.ts`: add `tce-main-street-auto-advance-turn` with
   `isAutoAdvanceTurnEnabled()` / `setAutoAdvanceTurnEnabled(enabled, storage?)`.
2. A single out-of-actions hook driven by the **post-action** path (producer decision
   Q1 = B): after an action resolves and its animations/audio complete, if the player's
   `actionsRemaining` has reached 0, then
   - setting **on** → invoke the same code path as the **End Turn** button, guarded by a
     once-per-turn latch and by the mode/phase guards in AC5;
   - setting **off** → `showOutOfActionsDialog()` once per turn.
   The existing per-site `actionsRemaining <= 0` legality guards
   (`MainStreetTurnControllerMarketActions`, `MainStreetTurnControllerDragDrop`,
   `MainStreetMarketSell`, `MainStreetMarketPurchase`) stay as they are — they remain the
   legality check for illegal attempts, not the trigger.
3. `MainStreetOverlayContent.showOutOfActionsDialog()` — explainer copy, an **End Turn**
   button, and an `[ ] Automatically end my turn when I run out of actions` checkbox that
   writes the preference when ticked.
4. Engine change (submodule): a generic extra-toggle hook in `SettingsPanelConfig` /
   `SettingsPanel` (and pass-through in `CardGameScene.initSettingsPanel`), wired from
   `MainStreetScene.initSettingsPanel` to the Main Street preference.
5. Tests and documentation as per AC6–AC7.

- `src/MainStreetPrefs.ts` — new `tce-main-street-auto-advance-turn` key + getter/setter,
  mirroring the premium-dialog preference pattern.

  `showBuyAndPlacePremiumDialog` (backdrop/box/element depths, checkbox + button,
  `overlayObjects` registration).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerUtils.ts` (or a new
  `src/scenes/MainStreetOutOfActions.ts`) — shared post-action out-of-actions helper +
  once-per-turn latch, called after an action's animation/audio settles.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerAnimation.ts` / `MainStreetAnimator*` — the
  animation-completion seam the trigger must wait on (the action is only "spent" for this
  purpose once its animations and audio have finished).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerMarketActions.ts` — call the post-action hook after
  each successful action resolution; leave the existing zero-action `flashError` guards
  untouched.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` — extend the `initSettingsPanel` override to pass the
  auto-advance toggle.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetLifecycleManagerLifecycle.ts` — panel initialisation site
  (`s.initSettingsPanel(DIFFICULTY_NAMES, 'Medium')`) if the toggle is wired there.
- `core/src/ui/SettingsPanel.ts`, `core/src/ui/CardGameScene.ts` — generic
  `extraToggles` config (engine repo, submodule pin bump via `npm run engine:sync`).
- `tests/main-street/main-street-prefs.test.ts` — preference unit tests.
- `tests/main-street/MainStreetAutoAdvanceTurn.browser.test.ts` (new) — auto-advance,
  dialog, checkbox persistence and guard browser tests.
- `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` (settings toggle inventory),
  `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` §6.0 Action Economy.

## Related work

- `MS-0MUUDWIXG009IB0W` — *Reject illegal moves before animation and action-point
  deduction* (the gate-then-animate pattern the helper should reuse).
- `MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41` — *End of Turn summary dialog* (the modal that follows a turn
  ending; auto-advance must still present it).
- `MS-0MVWMDMLE007I8E1` — *Harden Help/Settings browser tests* (Settings panel test
  conventions).
- `MS-0MT24X0SX007RLHN` — buy-and-place premium explainer dialog (the closest UI
  precedent, and the interaction that keeps zero-action play meaningful).
- `MS-0MT3IOPZB005LNAR` — action tooltip / action economy documentation.
- Duplicate check performed (`wl search` for "end turn", "action points", "settings") — no
  overlapping item satisfies these acceptance criteria.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk.** "Auto advance" invites extra wishes (auto-advance after N idle
  seconds, a countdown timer, auto-end in tutorial). These are recorded as follow-up work
  items, not folded in here.
- **Documented trade-off (producer decision Q1 = B).** Triggering on the spent-last-action
  moment means an opted-in player cannot use the action-free operations or the +50%
  same-turn buy-and-place after their final action — the turn simply ends. This is the
  intended behaviour of the opt-in setting; with the setting **off** the dialog is
  dismissible and those options stay reachable (AC4). If playtesting shows the trade-off
  is too harsh, a follow-up could defer the trigger while the hand has discardable cards or
  a premium placement is affordable — recorded as a follow-up, not in scope here.
- **Cross-repo coupling.** The Settings-panel toggle requires an engine change plus a
  submodule pin bump; the pin policy (`docs/dev/build-and-release.md`) means the engine
  commit must land on the engine `dev` branch before this repo's build is reproducible.
- **Re-entrancy.** Auto-advance runs from inside input handlers that already animate; it
  must be latched per turn, must wait for the triggering action's animations/audio to
  complete, and must not fire while `uiPhase === 'animating'` or while a dialog/overlay is
  open (turn-summary, loan offer, event choice).
- **Assumption:** the dialog is a one-off explainer (once per turn, and only while the
  setting is off), not a permanent nag on every illegal click.
- **Assumption:** the setting is global (per player), not per save game — it is a UI
  preference like Reduced Motion, not game state, so it is not serialised into saves.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

Intake was auto-dispatched with no interactive producer present, so the three decisions
below were recorded on the work item as a comment and the item flagged for producer review.
All three were subsequently answered by the producer (source: interactive reply,
2026-11-05) — **Q1 = B, Q2 = A, Q3 = A** — and the brief above reflects those answers.

- **Q1 — When exactly does the out-of-actions moment fire?** Options: (A) when the player
  attempts an action that costs an action point while at zero (replacing today's
  `flashError`); (B) immediately after the action that spends the last point resolves;
  (C) both (B for auto-advance, A for the dialog).
  **Recommended: A** — it preserves the deliberate zero-action affordances (discard, sell,
  research market, +50% same-turn buy-and-place) and gives one deterministic trigger that
  replaces the existing error path.
  **Answer (producer, 2026-11-05): B — "immediately after the action that spends the last
  action point resolves", with the qualification "and any animations/audio have completed".**
  Prior recommendation (A) superseded; the resulting trade-off is documented under *Risks
  and assumptions*.
- **Q2 — How should the setting be surfaced in the Settings panel?** Options: (A) a
  generic `extraToggles` hook in the engine's `SettingsPanel` (engine repo change + pin
  bump), consumed by Main Street; (B) a Main Street-owned settings overlay outside the
  engine panel; (C) engine-side `hasAutoAdvanceTurn` flag.
  **Recommended: A** — keeps the engine game-agnostic, reuses the existing panel, and is
  reusable by other games.
  **Answer (producer, 2026-11-05): A** — matches the recommendation.
- **Q3 — Which modes, and how often may the dialog appear?** Options: (A) solo + competitive
  human seats, suppressed in the tutorial and once per turn; (B) solo only; (C) all modes
  including the tutorial.
  **Recommended: A** — the tutorial's scripted `end-turn` steps would dead-end under
  auto-advance, and a per-turn nag would be hostile.
  **Answer (producer, 2026-11-05): A** — matches the recommendation.

# Improved activity log — filter by player / AI / all

## Problem statement

In competitive (human-vs-AI) play the Activity Log mixes the human seat's
actions, every AI seat's actions and shared turn/world events into one
undifferentiated stream, so a player cannot follow their own story or an
opponent's without reading every line. The log needs simple filter controls so
the player can view all activity, only their own activity, or only AI activity.

## Users

- **Competitive player** — wants to review what they did this game without
  wading through AI turns.
- **Competitive player** — wants to study an AI opponent's behaviour to learn
  from it.
- **Single-player / tutorial player** — must see an unchanged log; there is no
  AI seat to filter, so the controls must not appear.

Example user stories:

- As a competitive player, I want to show only my own activity so I can review
  my spending and income this game.
- As a competitive player, I want to show only AI activity so I can see how an
  opponent is building their street.
- As a competitive player, I want to return to the full log with one click so I
  can see the whole game in context.
- As a single-player player, I want the log to look and behave exactly as it
  does today.

## Acceptance Criteria

- In competitive mode the Activity Log panel presents three mutually exclusive
  filter controls — **All** (default), **You**, **AI** — and the active control
  is visually distinguishable from the inactive controls by more than colour
  alone (fill/stroke/text treatment).
- Selecting a filter re-renders the log to show only entries matching that
  filter, **without** mutating `state.activityLog`, changing entry order, or
  altering the persisted save data. Filtering is presentation-only.
- **Attribution is complete enough for the filter to be truthful**: every
  entry created by an acting seat's action (purchase, sell, upgrade, event play,
  hire, loan, income, reputation, etc.) is attributed to that seat, so
  filtering by You/AI never silently drops or mislabels a seat action.
- Turn headers and shared/turn-level entries (per-turn net summary, incident,
  market refresh/deal-in, week start, game-over) remain visible under every
  filter so turn structure and shared world events are never lost. A filter
  with no matching entries shows a clear, non-blank empty-state line.
- The filter controls are hidden and the log renders unchanged in
  single-player and tutorial modes; the selected filter survives turn end and
  UI refresh within a session and resets to **All** on scene restart / new game
  (never persisted to save data).
- Automated tests cover the pure filter/attribution predicate and the browser
  rendering: each filter shows exactly the expected entries, attribution is
  asserted for every action path, an empty filter shows the empty-state line,
  and no entry is lost or duplicated.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries
  (`docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md`,
  `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md`).
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Presentation-only** — filtering must never mutate game state, consume RNG,
  or change transcript/replay output (`state.activityLog` is read-only during
  render).
- **Single-player and tutorial are byte-for-byte unchanged** — no controls, no
  attribution, no seat prefixes (existing precedent: `resolveLogSeatColour`,
  `getSeatDisplayLabel` no-op with no roster or one seat).
- **Preserve the existing Activity Log contracts**: deferred-render ordering
  (`logDeferredUntilPhaseComplete`, MS-0MURBOD2E009SOM2), scene-creation reset
  (MS-0MV14JDUG000E1V6), auto-scroll/no-yank behaviour, word-wrap and the
  per-entry visibility optimisation.
- **Positioning follows the SLL layout authority** (`src/layouts/main-street.layout.json`,
  `src/scenes/MainStreetLayoutAdapter.ts`); the `activityLog` zone is
  ~300 × 218 px with a 22 px title bar, so the control treatment must fit
  without clipping or hiding the newest entry.
- **Colour is never the sole carrier of meaning** — the active filter must be
  readable without colour perception (text/fill/stroke differences).
- Reuse the shared `createActionButton` helper from `@ui/Renderer`; no new core
  engine infrastructure.
- Keep the change surgical: per-seat filters, type filters (gain/loss),
  filter persistence and a Settings toggle are **out of scope** (record them as
  linked follow-ups if they come up).

## Existing state

- `MainStreetState.activityLog: LogEntry[]` — each entry has `turn`, `text`,
  `type` (`gain` | `loss` | `neutral` | `turn-header`) and, in competitive mode,
  optional `seatId` / `seatLabel` / `seatColour`
  (`src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts`).
- `refreshLog()` (`src/scenes/MainStreetRendererHud.ts`) renders **all**
  entries into `logContentContainer`, applies per-entry visibility, recomputes
  `logTotalContentH` / `logMaxScroll` and honours the deferral gate and
  auto-scroll.
- The panel is built once in `createContainers` (`src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts`):
  `logContainer` → title bar (`'Activity Log'`, `LOG_TITLE_H = 22`) →
  `logContentContainer` → renderer-aware clip → wheel scroll.
- **Seat attribution is currently partial.** Only per-seat income/reputation
  entries use the seat overload `addLog(state, seatId, text, type)`
  (`src/MainStreetAdjacencyScoring.ts`). Most action entries (purchases, sells,
  upgrades, event plays, hires, loans) call the shared overload
  `addLog(state, text, type)` in `src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts`,
  `src/MainStreetMarketPurchase.ts`, `src/MainStreetMarketSell.ts`, etc., and
  therefore carry no `seatId`.
- Competitive mode is detected by the presence of `state.players` (absent in
  single-player); seat 0 controls the human (`controller === 'human'`, resolved
  by `findHumanSeatId`), every other seat is an AI (`AI 1`, `AI 2`, …).
- There is **no filter state** in the scene or the save shape today.

## Desired change

1. Add a presentation-only `logFilter` (`'all' | 'human' | 'ai'`) to the scene,
   defaulting to `'all'` and reset on scene creation.
2. Extend seat attribution so every entry produced by an acting seat's action
   carries that seat (`seatId` / `seatLabel` / `seatColour`); genuinely shared
   and turn-level entries stay unattributed.
3. Add three persistent filter controls to the Activity Log panel (compact row
   beneath the title bar), showing the active selection.
4. Filter the entry list in `refreshLog()` before rendering, recomputing content
   height and scroll bounds; keep shared/turn-level entries visible; show an
   empty-state line when a filter matches nothing.
5. Hide the controls (and render unchanged) when fewer than two seats exist
   (single-player / tutorial).
6. Cover the predicate, attribution and rendering with automated tests and
   update the docs.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` — build the persistent filter
  controls inside the Activity Log panel (row under the title bar).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererHud.ts` — filter entries in `refreshLog()`,
  recompute total content height/scroll bounds, empty-state line, ignore
  filtered-out entries in visibility and auto-scroll.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` — `logFilter` field (+ reset on scene
  creation) and any filter-control bookkeeping.
- `src/MainStreetStateLog.ts` — shared seat-attribution helper / overload used
  by action paths; keep the prefix legibility contract.
- `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts` — `LogFilter` type and any attribution fields.
- `src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts`, `src/MainStreetMarketPurchase.ts`,
  `src/MainStreetMarketSell.ts`, `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts`,
  `src/MainStreetLoans.ts`, `src/MainStreetChallenges.ts` — stamp the acting
  seat on action entries.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetConstants.ts` — filter-row height / control constants
  (derived from the SLL panel width, not hard-coded panel coordinates).
- `src/MainStreetLogFilter.ts` — pure filter predicate module (`LogFilter`,
  predicate, control-visibility helper).
- `tests/main-street/helpers/activity-log-harness.ts` — shared headless action
  driver and competitive scene boot helper.
- `tests/main-street/activity-log-filter.test.ts` — pure filter predicate and
  attribution coverage.
- `tests/main-street/activity-log-filter.browser.test.ts` — rendering: each
  filter, empty state, single-player/tutorial unchanged, scroll bounds.
- `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` — Activity Log section: filtering and
  attribution.
- `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` — panel/control treatment notes.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Attribution gap is the top risk.** If only per-seat income entries are
  attributed, a "You"/"AI" filter would hide most real actions and be
  misleading. **Producer confirmed (Q1 = A):** attribution is extended to all
  acting-seat entries before the filter ships, with tests on every action path.
- **Layout pressure.** The panel is 300 px wide with a 22 px title bar; a
  filter row reduces visible log height. Mitigation: derive the filter-row
  height from a constant and subtract it from `visibleH` so scroll bounds stay
  correct.
- **Deferred render interaction.** Filter changes made during end-of-turn
  deferral must apply on the next render, not force a render that violates the
  ordering contract.
- **Auto-scroll interaction.** A filter change alters max scroll; clamp the
  offset and preserve the player's "scrolled up" position, otherwise focus
  jumps unexpectedly.
- **Scope-creep risk.** Per-seat (AI 1 / AI 2) filtering, gain/loss type
  filters, persisting the filter across sessions and a Settings toggle are
  deliberately excluded; record them as linked follow-up work items rather than
  widening this item.
- **Assumption A (granularity).** "Player or AI ... all together" is
  interpreted as three buckets: **All / You / AI**, where "AI" groups every AI
  seat. Per-seat filtering is a separate future item.
- **Assumption B (persistence).** The selected filter lives in scene state
  only: it survives turns and UI refreshes, resets to **All** on scene
  restart / new game, and is not serialised into save data.
- **Assumption C (placement).** The controls are a compact row immediately
  beneath the existing title bar; the title text and title height are unchanged.
- **Assumption D.** The tutorial's existing highlight/hit-area expectations are
  preserved because the controls are hidden while the tutorial is active.

## Related work

- **MS-0MUWNTN8W006C7EF** — Identify different AI players (completed): added the
  seat label/colour prefix to log entries (`resolveLogSeatColour`,
  `getSeatDisplayLabel`), the attribution foundation this filter builds on.
- **MS-0MV14JDUG000E1V6** — Turn log no longer displays (completed): the log
  content regression and its scene-creation reset contract that must not
  regress.
- **MS-0MURBOD2E009SOM2** — Activity Log should not show log line until the
  results have been shown in the UI (completed): the deferred-render ordering
  contract that filtering must respect.
- **MS-0MV1BMMO900824N9** — Restore Activity Log rendering (completed):
  `refreshLog` deferral gate and count-based re-render; filtering changes the
  re-render trigger, so this contract is in scope.
- **MS-0MUTTVR5K002ZDUP** — Playable AI competitive mode (human vs AI)
  (completed): the mode in which the filter is visible and meaningful.
- Related docs: `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` (Activity Log section),
  `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` (play-panel treatment and seat colours).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions and answers

### Q1 — Attribution completeness

**Question:** Today only per-seat income/reputation entries carry a seat; most
play actions (purchases, sells, upgrades, event plays, hires, loans) are
unattributed. Should this item extend attribution so every acting-seat action
is stamped with that seat?

- (A) Yes — stamp the acting seat on all seat-action entries, then filter on
  complete attribution. *(Recommended)*
- (B) No — filter on the existing partial attribution only (accept that the
  filter will hide most player/AI actions).
- (C) Defer attribution to a separate blocking work item and land the filter
  afterwards.

**Recommended:** (A) — without complete attribution the filter is misleading and
would hide the very actions the player wants to review.

**Answer (producer, 2026-11-05): (A)** — extend attribution so every
acting-seat action is stamped with that seat. Source: producer reply to the
intake questions comment (`MS-C0MW3GO7A4005DYW8`).

### Q2 — Shared / unattributed entries under a filter

**Question:** What should happen to entries with no seat (turn headers, per-turn
net summary, incidents, market refresh, week start, game-over) when **You** or
**AI** is selected?

- (A) Always show them under every filter. *(Recommended)*
- (B) Hide them unless **All** is selected.
- (C) Show only turn headers and the per-turn net summary, hiding shared world
  events (incidents, market refresh).

**Recommended:** (A) — turn structure and shared world events affect every seat
and keep the filtered log readable.

**Answer (producer, 2026-11-05): (A)** — shared/turn-level entries (turn
headers, per-turn net summary, incidents, market refresh, week start,
game-over) stay visible under every filter. Source: producer reply to the
intake questions comment (`MS-C0MW3GO7A4005DYW8`).

### Q3 — Mode scope

**Question:** Single-player has no AI seats and no seat attribution. Should the
filter controls appear only in competitive mode?

- (A) Competitive only — hide the controls in single-player and tutorial and
  render the log unchanged. *(Recommended)*
- (B) All modes — show the controls everywhere (in single-player "AI" would be
  empty or undefined).
- (C) Single-player + competitive, hide only in the tutorial.

**Recommended:** (A) — there is nothing to filter without AI seats, and
single-player visuals stay unchanged.

**Answer (producer, 2026-11-05): (A)** — controls appear in competitive mode
only; single-player and tutorial render the log unchanged. Source: producer
reply to the intake questions comment (`MS-C0MW3GO7A4005DYW8`).

### Documented assumptions (non-blocking)

- **Assumption A (granularity)** — All / You / AI, with AI grouping every AI
  seat. Source: the item description ("player or ai, or ... all together").
- **Assumption B (persistence)** — session-only filter state; reset to All on
  scene restart / new game; not saved.
- **Assumption C (placement)** — compact filter row beneath the existing title
  bar, preserving the title text and height.
- **Assumption D (tutorial)** — controls hidden while the tutorial is active,
  preserving tutorial highlight/hit-area expectations.

### Research summary

- Read `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts` (`LogEntry`, `PlayerRecord`,
  `findHumanSeatId`), `src/MainStreetStateLog.ts` (seat overload and prefix
  legibility), `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererHud.ts` (`refreshLog`, deferral
  gate, scroll bounds), `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` (panel
  construction) and `src/scenes/MainStreetLayoutAdapter.ts` (SLL activityLog
  zone → 300 × 218).
- Audited every `addLog(` call site: 92 calls across 16 files; only
  `src/MainStreetAdjacencyScoring.ts` uses the seat overload for per-seat
  income/reputation. This is the evidence for the Q1 attribution gap.
- No filter state or filter UI exists in the scene, save shape or docs today;
  no duplicate or overlapping open work item was found.
- `find-related` automated report was run; its repo-file matches were
  `core/` docs with only generic keyword overlap and were not retained as
  related work.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MV1BMDU500878GN** – Add Activity Log regression test and pin introducing commit (completed)
- **MS-0MURBOD2E009SOM2** – Activity Log should not show log line until the results have been showin in the UI (completed)
- **MS-0MV1BMMO900824N9** – Restore Activity Log rendering (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: activity, add, allows, buttons, filtering (+4 more)
- `core/CHANGELOG.md` — matched: activity, add, buttons, improved, log (+2 more)
- `core/docs/core-engine/story-line.md` — matched: activity, add, buttons, filtering, log (+2 more)
